text:
Seth Jarvis has played 14 of Carolina's games and hasn't found his scoring touch in any of them. Two goals, 28 shots, 7.1% shooting, against a normal of about 13% by our numbers. For a player who scored 128 goals before turning 24, that's a slump, not a decline.

The assists have kept him useful: nine of his 11 points, and five in his last ten games. But the role has shrunk. He's averaged 16 minutes and 15 seconds, his ice time over the last ten is down more than two and a half minutes from before, and he has zero power-play points so far. Carolina is deep enough to win without him, which may be why nobody has panicked.

The good signs are small and specific. Cory Lavalette of the North State Journal had him among the best chances on one power play in Tampa, and his block started the rush for Jaccob Slavin's first goal of the year. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him 86th percentile for chances from the slot last season. Watch the shooting percentage. When it turns, our range still puts him at 15 to 29 goals.
